findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:69 — P2, confidence 100: Replacing the reactive website label with `{{model.website_name}}` leaves profile owners displaying the previous website's label after editing `model.website`, because `User.save()` only merges `self.set('bio_excerpt',data.user.bio_excerpt)` from the response (models/user.js.es6:210) and never refreshes the newly introduced derived field, so the visible label and href disagree until the model is reloaded.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — P2, confidence 100: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` treats independently registered `customer.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk` as the same domain, so a profile URL such as `https://customer.co.uk/user` incorrectly receives the same-domain full-path presentation on `forum.co.uk` because removing one label confuses a public suffix with a shared domain.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — P1, confidence 100: `def include_website_name` and `website.present?` fail to propagate the existing `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` exclusion to `website_name`, so anonymous visitors receive and render a TL0 user's otherwise hidden website host/path; the strongest counterargument is that `website` remains excluded, but `website_name` reads the profile directly and the template now renders on `model.website_name` alone.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — P2, confidence 75: `if website_host == discourse_host` omits case-insensitive hostname matching, so a profile website `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on instance `example.com` displays only `EXAMPLE.COM` and loses the required same-domain path; the strongest counterargument is that the sibling/parent branches also compare domains, but both remain case-sensitive and the two-label example bypasses the sibling branch entirely.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — P2, confidence 75: `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` works for ASCII URLs but silently drops a stored browser-usable website such as `https://example.com/café` because Ruby raises `URI::InvalidURIError` and `{{#if model.website_name}}` then hides the entire website from profile visitors; the strongest counterargument is that rejecting malformed URLs avoids rendering broken links, but this URL renders in browsers and the previous `website.split("/")[2]` displayed its hostname, so swallowing the parser failure removes a working link instead of providing a fallback.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:69 — P2 advisory, confidence 100: the shared fixture `user.user_profile.website = 'http://example.com/user'` leaves both outcomes of the new sibling-subdomain branch unexercised, and replacing that branch with `website_host` preserves all three added examples while dropping `/user` for profile viewers seeing `http://www.example.com/user` on `forums.example.com`; the strongest counterargument is that the examples cover exact, parent, and unrelated domains, but none reaches the equal-depth subdomain condition, so subsequent changes to the sibling comparison have no regression protection.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:69 — P2, confidence 100: Replacing the reactive website label with `{{model.website_name}}` leaves profile owners displaying the previous website's label after editing `model.website`, because `User.save()` only merges `self.set('bio_excerpt',data.user.bio_excerpt)` from the response (models/user.js.es6:210) and never refreshes the newly introduced derived field, so the visible label and href disagree until the model is reloaded.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: the diff shows that `website_name` is now computed server-side and returned in the serializer, but when a user edits their profile, the `User.save()` method (referenced in models/user.js.es6:210) only merges specific fields like `bio_excerpt` from the response. The new `website_name` field would not be automatically refreshed after saving because it's a derived field computed from `website` on the server side. The template now uses `model.website_name` directly instead of the previously computed property `websiteName` that was reactive to `model.website` changes. This means after editing the website, the displayed `website_name` could be stale until the model is reloaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — P2, confidence 100: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` treats independently registered `customer.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk` as the same domain, so a profile URL such as `https://customer.co.uk/user` incorrectly receives the same-domain full-path presentation on `forum.co.uk` because removing one label confuses a public suffix with a shared domain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the domain comparison logic at line 146. The code `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` compares domains by removing the first label and checking if the rest matches. For domains like 'customer.co.uk' and 'forum.co.uk', this would compare 'co.uk' == 'co.uk' which is true, incorrectly treating them as related domains. This is a legitimate edge case bug where public suffixes (like .co.uk) are confused with shared parent domains, causing incorrect full-path presentation for unrelated domains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — P1, confidence 100: `def include_website_name` and `website.present?` fail to propagate the existing `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` exclusion to `website_name`, so anonymous visitors receive and render a TL0 user's otherwise hidden website host/path; the strongest counterargument is that `website` remains excluded, but `website_name` reads the profile directly and the template now renders on `model.website_name` alone.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at the diff, the serializer adds `website_name` to the attributes list (line 43) and defines `include_website_name` (lines 156-158) which only checks `website.present?`. However, the existing `website` method is listed under `untrusted_attributes` (visible at line 43 where `website` already exists), which means it has restriction logic via `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The new `website_name` attribute bypasses this restriction because its `include_website_name` method doesn't check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The template now renders based on `model.website_name` alone (line 66-72 in the template), so anonymous visitors could see website information for TL0 users that should be hidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — P2, confidence 75: `if website_host == discourse_host` omits case-insensitive hostname matching, so a profile website `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on instance `example.com` displays only `EXAMPLE.COM` and loses the required same-domain path; the strongest counterargument is that the sibling/parent branches also compare domains, but both remain case-sensitive and the two-label example bypasses the sibling branch entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the hostname comparison `website_host == discourse_host` is case-sensitive. Looking at the diff, line 141 shows `if website_host == discourse_host` which compares strings directly. If a user enters 'https://EXAMPLE.COM/user' and the instance is 'example.com', URI parsing would give 'EXAMPLE.COM' as the host, and the equality check would fail (since 'EXAMPLE.COM' != 'example.com'). This would cause the code to fall through to the else branches, potentially returning just the hostname without the path when it should include the path for same-domain URLs. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, so this is a real edge case bug. The tests don't cover this case either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — P2, confidence 75: `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` works for ASCII URLs but silently drops a stored browser-usable website such as `https://example.com/café` because Ruby raises `URI::InvalidURIError` and `{{#if model.website_name}}` then hides the entire website from profile visitors; the strongest counterargument is that rejecting malformed URLs avoids rendering broken links, but this URL renders in browsers and the previous `website.split("/")[2]` displayed its hostname, so swallowing the parser failure removes a working link instead of providing a fallback.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new code uses `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` which will return nil for URLs with non-ASCII characters (like 'https://example.com/café') due to URI::InvalidURIError. When website_host is nil, the method returns early with `return if website_host.nil?`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` not whether website_name was successfully computed. This means a valid browser-usable URL that was previously displayed (the old code used simple string splitting `website.split("/")[2]` which would work for such URLs) will now have its website_name hidden. The diff shows the template uses `{{#if model.website_name}}` to conditionally display the website, so this is a regression that removes working functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:69 — P2 advisory, confidence 100: the shared fixture `user.user_profile.website = 'http://example.com/user'` leaves both outcomes of the new sibling-subdomain branch unexercised, and replacing that branch with `website_host` preserves all three added examples while dropping `/user` for profile viewers seeing `http://www.example.com/user` on `forums.example.com`; the strongest counterargument is that the examples cover exact, parent, and unrelated domains, but none reaches the equal-depth subdomain condition, so subsequent changes to the sibling comparison have no regression protection.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a missing test case. Looking at the diff, the `website_name` method in user_serializer.rb has a specific branch for when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and both have more than 2 parts (the sibling subdomain case, e.g., www.example.com vs forum.example.com). The three test cases added cover: (1) unrelated domains (discourse.org vs example.com), (2) exact match (example.com vs example.com), and (3) parent domain (forums.example.com vs example.com). None of these tests exercise the sibling subdomain branch where both hosts have equal depth > 2. This is a legitimate gap in test coverage for newly added logic, making it an important non-bug finding.
